answer: Each PoA identity must complete a Wesolowski VDF: sequential modular squarings, with each result required to compute the next. GPUs cannot parallelize the steps of one instance to eliminate its delay; clones may run concurrently, but each requires separate work and elapsed time. A verifier checks the opal-tagged transcript against the kernel’s challenge and accepts the relic-like proof only if valid. This raises the cost of Sybil identities, without making them impossible.
